tasks.title: Step 10: History UI, AI assistant & Docker delivery
tasks.body: Finish the last documented step: the history modal with a working side-by-side diff, the BYOK AI assistant and the one-click error fix, and a Docker image that serves the API, the client and a real LaTeX-to-PDF compile. Verify with the three-headed protocol (vitest, tsc --noEmit, runtime probe) and tag checkpoint-step-10-full-delivery.

tasks.title: Step 12: Share links that actually open a project
tasks.body: Make the /p/{id}?token=... deep link work. The server minted share links and the API and WebSocket understood share tokens, but the client had no route for /p/ — a co-editor following a link landed on the sign-in page and could not get in. Add the deep-link handling to the client, and accept a share token carried as a bearer so the browser can make requests with it. Verified with scripts/share-probe.mjs against a running server.

history.note: Share links work end to end: client deep link, bearer share token, runtime probe. PR #1.

tasks.title: Step 13: a usable editor, and bibliographies that build
tasks.body:
Make the editor usable and make biblatex documents build.

The reader was told "the request failed" where a TeX error was available, the build ran when nobody asked for it, the main file was a guess, the project could not be renamed, and a biblatex document never built.

Done:
- The client shows the compile error, with the file and the line.
- The build is a button the reader presses, with an automatic toggle.
- The main file is set in the interface and stored with the project, and an imported project has its entry point detected.
- A project can be renamed.
- The ACM sample's .bib is repaired (duplicate entries, accent convention).
- The server is biber-capable, with the version pairing pinned and proved at build time.
- Sharing works over the public internet through a cloudflared quick tunnel; npm run share:public.

Verified: typecheck clean, 493 tests passing, build green, both docker biblatex gates pass, the running container compiles a biblatex document, 16/16 share checks, and the public tunnel serves the deep link, the API and the collaboration socket.

PR #2.
